$comment: Entry schema for contributes.jdtlsBundles (process plugins that declare the shell capability, manifest apiVersion 2). Host validation lives in backend/plugin/contrib_jdtls_bundles.go (install) and jdtls_bundles_trust.go (confirmation and loading). Each entry names one jar inside the plugin package that the built-in Java language server (jdtls) loads as an OSGi bundle, and the jdtls commands that jar registers, plus optional dependencies: at most {{limits.dependenciesMax}} library jars that register no commands, under the same path rules, loaded and confirmed as one group with the entry's jar (if one is missing or changed, none of the plugin's jars loads until the user confirms again). path must be ${pluginRoot}/<relative>.jar: a regular file inside the package (no .. segments, no symlink leaving the package) of at most {{limits.jarMaxBytes}} bytes. Loading a jar runs the plugin's code inside the jdtls process, which sees every source file of the project: the host adds a plugin's jars to jdtls only after the user confirms them (fingerprint: plugin id, version, development generation, each jar's SHA-256 and its sorted commands, dependency jars included) in every approval mode, re-hashes them before every jdtls start and, if any jar of the plugin is missing, oversized or changed, loads none of the plugin's jars until the user confirms the whole set again. All of a plugin's jars together (every entry, dependencies included) are at most {{limits.bundleBytesMax}} bytes. A running jdtls keeps the jars it started with; when the confirmed set changes (enable, disable, upgrade, uninstall, confirmation) the host asks the user to restart the Java language service and never restarts it on its own. A command may be declared once per plugin; a command already declared by an earlier installed plugin (persisted install order) rejects the later plugin's entry, which the install preview reports. Stopping the plugin process does not change the loaded jars. Plugins may only call the commands they declare. Confirmations are kept for at most {{limits.trustEntriesMax}} entries per plugin, never exported, and deleted on uninstall and Clear Plugin Data.
description: jdtls bundles: jars inside the plugin package that the built-in Java language server loads after the user confirms them, with the jdtls commands they register.

path.description: ${pluginRoot}/<relative path>.jar inside the plugin package, at most {{limits.jarMaxBytes}} bytes.

commands.description: jdtls workspace/executeCommand ids the jar registers; unique within the plugin and across installed plugins.

dependencies.description: Library jars the jar needs that register no commands, each ${pluginRoot}/<relative path>.jar inside the plugin package of at most {{limits.jarMaxBytes}} bytes. They load, hash and are confirmed together with the entry's jar; a jar may appear once per plugin.
